thread.title: Amazon Looking To Challenge Apple In Payments War - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Bluesea Research
title: Amazon Looking To Challenge Apple In Payments War - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
Amazon ( AMZN ) is aggressively pursuing market share growth in mobile payments. WSJ reports that Amazon is asking gas stations and restaurants to offer Amazon Pay options to customers. Amazon also will be increasing the presence in brick and mortar stores with whom it does not directly compete for retail sales. On the other hand, Apple ( AAPL ) also is looking to gain a decisive market share for its own digital wallet platform.
A recent Bloomberg report mentioned that Apple Pay is in second position, behind PayPal (NASDAQ: PYPL ), in number of active users using the digital wallet. However, Amazon has a significant benefit due to its online retail business, Prime membership and further growth in the brick and mortar space. Amazon also is investing heavily to increase the market share of Amazon Pay in international regions. As the mobile payments market matures, we should see two or three major players grabbing a big chunk of the market share.
Amazon takes aggressive steps Amazon Pay has been around since 2007. However, Amazon has only recently started making aggressive investments to increase the market share of its digital wallet. It's now asking brick and mortar stores with whom it does not compete to allow Amazon Pay options for customers. It's not clear whether Amazon Pay will use QR codes or NFC technology which is used by Apple Pay. QR codes are generally preferred by smaller business owners as they can print and tape the codes without any big investments in NFC terminals.
Amazon already has made huge investments in increasing the acceptance of its digital wallet in international markets. In India, Amazon has spent INR 10.15 billion or approximately $145 million in 2018 to improve the market share of Amazon Pay.
Source: Bloomberg
Currently, Amazon Pay does not rank among the top players within digital payments in US. At the same time, the overall penetration of iPhones is still increasing on a healthy pace in US. Despite low unit sales growth, the installed base has increased by double digits on YoY basis in the US in recent quarter.
Source: CIRP
A major reason for this growth is the high resale value of iPhones which allows users to purchase older models at lower prices. A higher market share of iPhones will certainly help in expanding the target audience of Apple Pay within US. But Amazon has a number of structural advantages which can allow rapid growth of its digital wallet.
Similarity with other markets Digital wallets have seen slower acceptance in the US compared to other regions. The main reason is the high penetration of credit cards within US. In other regions like China, the penetration of credit cards is much lower which has helped in the rapid growth of mobile payment platforms like Alibaba’s ( BABA ) Alipay and Tencent’s Wechat Pay.
In China, Alipay has a market share of 54% which closely corresponds to the market share of Alibaba in the e-commerce segment. According to eMarketer , Amazon's share of e-commerce is 49%. Customers buying goods on Alibaba’s e-commerce platform have to use Alipay and cannot use rival Wechat Pay for payments. Tencent has close relationships and investments in other e-commerce players like JD ( JD ) and Pinduoduo ( PDD ). These e-commerce platforms do not allow payments through Alipay.
At the same time, the penetration of digital wallets from smartphone manufacturers is very low. Apple has tried to improve the market share of Apple Pay in China but has low single-digit share. It has even allowed payments through Alipay within its own retail stores in China.
Advantages with Amazon Amazon is significantly behind other players in terms of market share of its digital wallet in the US. But if the future digital wallet trend in the US follows the trajectory we saw in China then retail giants should have the upper hand.
Source: WSJ
A recent CIRP report shows that Amazon’s Prime membership is close to hitting the 100 million mark. These members purchase an average of $1,400 of goods every year. Amazon can provide attractive discount options to customers for using its own digital wallet against other competitors.
Source: CIRP , WP
Besides e-commerce, Amazon is aggressively moving into the brick and mortar space. It already has a massive store base through Whole Foods stores and is looking to expand Amazon Go stores. In September, Bloomberg reported that Amazon is planning to have 3,000 Amazon Go stores by 2021. This will further increase the share of customer transactions made through Amazon’s platform. In almost all the channels controlled by Amazon, it would be aggressively trying to make the customers use Amazon Pay.
The recent move to attract gas stations, restaurants and smaller retailers to use Amazon Pay shows the determination of Amazon to gain a big market share in digital payments segment.
Challenges faced by Apple Apple also has a number of advantages which should help it in improving the market share of its digital wallet. Amazon is considered the chief rival by most of the retailers. If they want an alternative choice for digital payments, they would likely choose Apple Pay. Apple also has a huge installed base in the US which helps in expanding peer-to-peer transfer. A higher market share for Apple Pay will help the company in improving the moat around its profitable devices like iPhones and smartwatches.
However, we need to note that most iPhone users would probably be using Amazon for their purchases. Amazon will not allow these transactions to be done through Apple Pay. Hence, even the most prolific users of Apple devices would need an Amazon Pay account for their purchases on Amazon’s platform. An Amazon Pay account also would help them make cash transfers to Android users.
Amazon has invested close to $150 million in improving the market share of Amazon Pay in India. Amazon’s business in India is a small fraction of its US business. In my opinion, we should see significant investments by Amazon in its digital wallet platform in US over the next two years.
A rapidly growing digital wallet market share should become one of the biggest moats for Amazon and also improve the long-term growth potential for the company. Prime membership base, big e-commerce market share and future growth in brick and mortar segment provides Amazon with several advantages to gain a decisive market share in the digital wallet segment within US. On the other hand, Apple Pay faces an uphill task as it will not be allowed by Amazon on its platform. Usability of Apple Pay also is limited as transactions with Android users is not possible.
Investor Takeaway Digital wallet will be a major battleground over the next few quarters for Amazon, Apple and other big players. Amazon has an advantage in this segment as it has a significant Prime membership base which can be given attractive discounts to use Amazon Pay. Amazon also can restrict the usage of other payment options on its platform. In the past year, Amazon has invested heavily to improve the traction of Amazon Pay in international regions. Over the next few quarters, we could see massive investments by Amazon in improving the market share of Amazon Pay in US.
Apple provides a good alternative to Amazon Pay for retailers looking for other options. But its usage is limited as Android users cannot make transactions on Apple Pay. International markets also have shown that a platform agnostic option is better suited for digital wallet which reduces the attraction of smartphone manufacturers like Apple.
